title: GROUP PREFERENCE OPTIMIZATION: FEW-SHOT ALIGNMENT OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the alignment of the language model's predicted probability distributions over multiple-choice survey answers against ground-truth human survey data from 14 different countries using the GlobalOpinionQA dataset, measured via Jensen-Shannon Distance.

Measuring the Wasserstein Distance between the model's predicted answer distributions and the actual survey responses of different political ideologies (Liberal, Conservative, Moderate) and parties (Democrat, Republican) using the OpinionQA dataset.
Comparing the model's predicted opinion distributions on multiple-choice survey questions to the survey responses of various racial groups (Black, White, Asian, Hispanic) using the OpinionQA dataset.

Evaluating the alignment between the model's generated survey answer distributions and the actual preferences of different religious groups (Protestant, Jewish, Hindu, Atheist, Muslim) using the OpinionQA dataset.
Measuring the alignment of model outputs with the survey response distributions of different income brackets (e.g., >$100K+ vs <$30K) using the OpinionQA dataset.
Comparing the model's predicted opinion distributions to the survey responses of groups with different educational backgrounds (College graduate/some postgrad vs. Less than high school).
Evaluating the alignment between the model's multiple-choice survey answer distributions and the actual preferences of male and female demographic groups.
Measuring the alignment of the language model's outputs with the survey response distributions of individuals from different regions within the US (Northeast, South) using the OpinionQA dataset.
